title: Migraine-spectrum disorder / silent migraine
description: Migraine can produce profound fatigue, sleepiness, brain fog, nausea, photophobia/phonophobia, autonomic symptoms, and visual symptoms even with little or no headache.
why_it_fits: Stereotyped facial/head pain, light/sound sensitivity, behind-the-eyes sensations, nausea, neck involvement, fluctuating episodes, and improvement after sleep all fit a migraine-spectrum pattern.

title: Migraine with prominent hypothalamic/autonomic involvement
description: A migraine phenotype in which sleep/wake, temperature, autonomic, and arousal symptoms are more prominent than head pain.
why_it_fits: Could unify irresistible sleep, brain fog, hot/cold sensations, nausea, sensory sensitivity, and occasional mild headache.

title: POTS / dysautonomia / orthostatic intolerance
description: Abnormal regulation of heart rate, vascular tone, and blood distribution when upright; often worsened by heat, meals, or exertion.
why_it_fits: A prior home orthostatic test showed heart rate rising from 89 supine to 120 after 10 minutes standing. Heat intolerance, sweating, air hunger, heavy limbs, and improvement with rest also fit.

title: Primary sleep disorder — especially OSA/UARS
description: Repeated sleep disruption from airway obstruction or increased respiratory effort can cause severe daytime sleepiness despite apparently adequate sleep.
why_it_fits: Irresistible naps despite stimulant medication and caffeine are significant. Typical sleep duration is often 6.5–7 hours, and consumer watch data cannot reliably exclude apnea.

title: Idiopathic hypersomnia (IH)
description: A neurologic hypersomnolence disorder characterized by excessive sleep need, long naps, and marked sleep inertia.
why_it_fits: Long 90–120+ minute involuntary naps, severe grogginess if awakened early, and sleepiness that can overpower stimulants resemble IH.

title: Perimenopause / hormonal instability
description: Hormonal fluctuations can worsen migraine, sleep quality, autonomic symptoms, temperature regulation, cognition, and mood symptoms.
why_it_fits: Age and symptom pattern make hormonal instability plausible, and it could amplify migraine and sleep problems without explaining everything by itself.

title: Histamine as a migraine/autonomic trigger
description: Histamine exposure or mast-cell signaling may lower migraine threshold or worsen autonomic symptoms without requiring mast-cell activation syndrome.
why_it_fits: A period of severe sleepiness overlapped with daily yogurt intake and improved after stopping it; food-related flares have also been considered.

title: Systemic nickel allergy syndrome (SNAS)
description: Systemic exposure to nickel can provoke dermatitis and sometimes gastrointestinal or systemic symptoms in sensitized people.
why_it_fits: Positive nickel/cobalt patch testing and recurrent characteristic rash support genuine nickel sensitivity. The connection to profound sleepiness is less certain.
confidence: High for rash; Low–Moderate for sleepiness

title: Medication / drug-interaction effects
description: Medications can alter sleep architecture, arousal, blood pressure, autonomic function, and caffeine metabolism.
why_it_fits: Fluvoxamine affects caffeine metabolism; verapamil may affect blood pressure/autonomic responses; stimulants and other psychiatric medications complicate the arousal picture.

title: Binocular vision dysfunction / ocular motor problem
description: Eye alignment or convergence problems can provoke visual strain, headache, dizziness, and migraine.
why_it_fits: An eye has been observed drifting while reading, alongside behind-the-eye discomfort and sensory symptoms.

title: Cervicogenic migraine / cervical input
description: Neck pathology can activate trigeminal and migraine pathways and contribute to head or facial pain.
why_it_fits: MRI shows C5–6 disease with severe right foraminal stenosis, while neck, jaw, and facial symptoms have often occurred together.

title: Recurrent/occult UTI or other infection
description: Infection can cause fatigue, sleepiness, and cognitive symptoms even when urinary symptoms are subtle.
why_it_fits: Long history of recurrent, difficult-to-culture UTIs and resistant organisms means infection could explain individual crashes, including current episodes.
confidence: Moderate for individual episodes; Low as unifying diagnosis

title: Mast cell activation syndrome (MCAS)
description: Inappropriate mast-cell mediator release causing episodic symptoms across multiple organ systems.
why_it_fits: Rashes, itching, gastrointestinal symptoms, heat intolerance, and some food associations can fit. Against it: inconsistent response to low-histamine approaches and lack of a strong recurrent multisystem allergic pattern.

title: ME/CFS
description: A disorder characterized especially by post-exertional malaise, impaired recovery, cognitive dysfunction, and unrefreshing sleep.
why_it_fits: Fatigue, brain fog, and orthostatic symptoms fit superficially, but clear delayed post-exertional malaise has not been a dominant feature.

title: Fibromyalgia / central sensitization
description: Altered pain processing associated with widespread pain, fatigue, sleep disturbance, headaches, and cognitive symptoms.
why_it_fits: Earlier combinations of aches, fatigue, sleep issues, GI symptoms, and headaches fit, but newer migraine/autonomic clues are more specific.

title: Small-fiber neuropathy
description: Dysfunction or damage of small sensory and autonomic nerve fibers, sometimes associated with POTS.
why_it_fits: Could connect autonomic symptoms with sensory and temperature-regulation complaints, but classic persistent burning neuropathic symptoms have not been prominent.

title: Systemic autoimmune disease — lupus/Sjögren's/etc.
description: Systemic inflammatory disease can cause fatigue, neurologic symptoms, Raynaud-type symptoms, and rashes.
why_it_fits: Raynaud/chilblain-like symptoms and rashes made this reasonable to investigate, but negative ANA testing and rash biopsies not showing lupus reduce the fit.

title: Intracranial hypertension (IIH)
description: Elevated intracranial pressure can cause headache, pressure behind the eyes, visual symptoms, pulsatile tinnitus, and sometimes sixth-nerve palsy.
why_it_fits: Eye-pressure sensations, headache, and eye drift make it worth considering, but papilledema, typical transient visual obscurations, pulsatile tinnitus, or elevated opening pressure have not been established.

title: Hypothyroidism
description: Low thyroid hormone can cause fatigue, sleepiness, cold intolerance, cognitive slowing, and weight changes.
why_it_fits: It belongs in the differential for profound fatigue and is easy to screen for, although the episodic migraine/autonomic pattern is not especially characteristic.
confidence: Low if prior thyroid testing normal; otherwise unresolved

title: Iron/B12/vitamin-D deficiency or anemia
description: Nutritional deficiencies or anemia can cause fatigue, cognitive problems, exercise intolerance, and sometimes neurologic symptoms.
why_it_fits: Common and treatable causes of fatigue that should not be overlooked, though they do not explain the distinctive episodic migraine/sleep-attack pattern well.

title: Adrenal insufficiency
description: Inadequate cortisol production can cause severe fatigue, GI symptoms, orthostatic hypotension, and poor stress tolerance.
why_it_fits: Fatigue, nausea, and orthostatic-type symptoms overlap, but several stronger classic clues have not been prominent.

title: Post-viral syndrome / Long COVID
description: Persistent autonomic, neuroimmune, and cognitive dysfunction after infection.
why_it_fits: Could theoretically cause dysautonomia and fatigue, but no compelling infection-to-onset relationship has emerged.

title: Psychiatric stress / autistic-ADHD burnout
description: Chronic sensory, cognitive, and emotional load can markedly increase exhaustion and reduce resilience.
why_it_fits: Stress and sensory load may worsen symptoms, but involuntary naps, autonomic findings, photophobia, and stereotyped physical episodes make this inadequate as a sole explanation.
confidence: Moderate as amplifier; Low as primary cause

title: Narcolepsy type 2
description: A neurologic hypersomnolence disorder involving abnormal REM regulation, without cataplexy.
why_it_fits: Sleep attacks despite stimulant medication keep it in the sleep-medicine differential, but classic REM-related features have not been prominent.

title: Seizure disorder
description: Focal neurologic episodes can sometimes cause altered awareness followed by pronounced fatigue.
why_it_fits: Considered because some attacks are neurologically unusual, but the long, fluctuating, trigger-responsive, migraine-like episodes are less typical of seizures.

title: TIA / cerebrovascular episodes
description: Temporary focal cerebral ischemia causing transient neurologic deficits.
why_it_fits: Initially worth considering for unusual neurologic symptoms, but the recurrent stereotyped course and migraine features make this a poor global explanation.

title: Primary CNS autoimmune/inflammatory disease
description: Inflammation involving the brain or central nervous system can cause cognitive, autonomic, or sleep/wake abnormalities.
why_it_fits: Broad neurologic symptoms once made this part of a wide differential, but the long fluctuating history without progressive objective neurologic decline makes it less persuasive.
